title: III–IV. OT obscurely by just interpretation: Sadducees' marriage reductio; Abraham–Isaac–Jacob
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): (2) by opposing a new argument: Concerning ye resurrection, Have you not read what stood as said to you by God: I am ye God belonging toward Abraham, ye God belonging toward Isaac, plus ye God belonging toward Jacob? But Christ answers (1) by denying such that consequence, because in ye resurrection marriages cease (Luke 20:34 more fully); 25:5. They prove ye consequence out from Moses' law, Deut. Therefore so stands as ye antecedent. But ye consequent stands as absurd plus against ye law belonging toward nature. Luke 20:27: ye Sadducees tried to defend their opinion against Christ plus to overthrow ye resurrection he asserted together with an argument to absurdity: If there stands as a resurrection belonging toward ye dead, a great confusion belonging toward marriages will arise, so such that seven will be husbands belonging toward one woman. More obscurely by just interpretation it stands as demonstrated when a firm consequence stands as drawn out from a saying belonging toward ye Old Testament. IV. || From ye Old Testament it stands as demonstrated either more obscurely, by just interpretation, or more clearly, by evident diction. III.
pass_b_english: III. From the Old Testament it is demonstrated either more obscurely, by just interpretation, or more clearly, by evident diction.

IV. More obscurely by just interpretation it is demonstrated when a firm consequence is drawn from a saying of the Old Testament. Luke 20:27: the Sadducees tried to defend their opinion against Christ and to overthrow the resurrection he asserted with an argument to absurdity: If there is a resurrection of the dead, a great confusion of marriages will arise, so that seven will be husbands of one woman. But the consequent is absurd and against the law of nature. Therefore so is the antecedent. They prove the consequence from Moses' law, Deut. 25:5. But Christ answers (1) by denying that consequence, because in the resurrection marriages cease (Luke 20:34 more fully); (2) by opposing a new argument: Concerning the resurrection, Have you not read what was said to you by God: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
source_text: III. E V.T. demonstratur vel obscurius, per justam interpretationem, vel clarius, per evidentem dictionem. IV. Obscurius per justam interpretationem demonstratur, quando firma consequentia e dicto V.T. deducitur. Luc. 20.v.27. Sadducaei opinionem suam contra Christum defendere & resurrectionem a Christo assertam destruere conabantur argumento ducente ad absurdum: Si est resurrectio mortuorum, orietur magna confusio matrimoniorum, ita ut unius mulieris septem futuri sint mariti. Atqui absurdum est consequens & contra jus naturae. Ergo & antecedens. Consequentiam probant e lege Mosis Deut. 25.v.5. Christus vero respondet, 1. negando illam consequentiam, addita ratione, quia in resurrectione nuptiae cessant, id quod plenius expressit Lucas cap. 20.v.34. 2. Novum argumentum opponendo, qua suam sententiam confirmat, De resurrectione, inquiens, non legistis, quod vobis dictum est a Deo dicente: Ego sum Deus Abrahami, Deus Isaaci, & Deus Jacobi?
